name: What section 15(2) ADDS to the value of supply
definition: Section 15(2) lists five amounts the value of supply shall include, (a) to (e). They are additions to the transaction value, not alternatives to it, and they are mandatory — the sub-section says 'shall include'. (a) other statutory levies charged separately, with the four GST Acts carved out. (b) an amount the supplier was liable to pay but the recipient incurred, and which is not already in the price. (c) incidental expenses including commission and packing, and anything the supplier charges for anything done at or before delivery. (d) interest or late fee or penalty for delayed payment of any consideration. (e) subsidies directly linked to the price, other than subsidies provided by the Central Government and State Governments. An Explanation to the sub-section places a subsidy in the value of the supplier who RECEIVES it.
why_it_exists: The invoice total and the taxable value are different numbers, and s.15(2) is the whole of the difference on the additive side. Every limb names an amount a bookkeeper would naturally post somewhere other than sales — a recovery, a reimbursement, finance income, a grant. Left off the base, each one understates output tax on every invoice that carries it.
inputs: taxes, duties, cesses, fees and charges charged separately on the invoice, and the law each is levied under
amounts the supplier was liable to pay in relation to the supply that the recipient incurred instead
whether such an amount is already included in the price actually paid or payable
incidental expenses charged by the supplier, including commission and packing
amounts charged for anything done by the supplier at the time of, or before, delivery of goods or supply of services
interest, late fee or penalty charged for delayed payment of any consideration
subsidies received, who provided them, and whether they are directly linked to the price
outputs: the amount to be added under s.15(2)(a)
the amount to be added under s.15(2)(b)
the amount to be added under s.15(2)(c)
the amount to be added under s.15(2)(d)
the amount to be added under s.15(2)(e)
for each limb, an explicit NIL where the limb was considered and does not apply
preconditions: a transaction value exists under s.15(1) (GST-VAL-TRANSACTION-VALUE), or a value has been determined under the Rules to which the same additions apply
exceptions: s.15(2)(a) excludes tax charged under this Act, the State Goods and Services Tax Act, the Union Territory Goods and Services Tax Act and the Goods and Services Tax (Compensation to States) Act — GST is not charged on GST
s.15(2)(b) applies only where the amount is NOT already included in the price actually paid or payable — adding it twice is the error the limb's own words guard against
s.15(2)(e) excludes subsidies provided by the Central Government and State Governments
rule 33 — a payment made as a pure agent is excluded from value even though it looks like an incidental expense under s.15(2)(c) (GST-VAL-PURE-AGENT)
rule 32A — Kerala Flood Cess is not included in the value determined in terms of section 15
UNKNOWN — notifications made under the Act and the Rules are not held locally. A notification can narrow or displace a limb without the section or rule text changing.

common_mistakes: taking the invoice total as the value without walking all five limbs
excluding packing and commission as recoveries — s.15(2)(c) names commission and packing expressly
treating interest on a late-paid invoice as finance income outside GST — s.15(2)(d) puts it in the value of the supply
treating a late fee or a penalty for delayed payment as a damages receipt outside GST — s.15(2)(d) names late fee and penalty alongside interest
assuming every subsidy is excluded — only Central and State Government subsidies are, and only those directly linked to the price were ever in scope
putting a subsidy into the value of the wrong party — the Explanation puts it in the value of the supplier who receives it
charging GST on the GST shown separately — the four GST Acts are carved out of s.15(2)(a), other statutory levies are not
treating a limb as inapplicable silently instead of recording a considered NIL
legal_references: CGST Act 2017, s.15(2), Explanation — whose value a subsidy enters
icai_references: UNKNOWN — whether an amount added by s.15(2) is also revenue for accounting purposes is a separate question under AS 9 and was not determined here
gst_references: CGST Rules 2017, rule 33 — the pure agent exclusion, which removes an amount s.15(2)(c) would otherwise reach
UNKNOWN — source is the Act as updated 31-08-2021; later amendments not held locally
evidence_required: the tax invoice showing every separately charged line and the law each levy arises under
the contract or purchase order, to identify obligations of the supplier discharged by the recipient
the debit note or interest advice for any delayed-payment charge
the subsidy sanction document naming the provider and the basis of the subsidy
confidence_factors: weak when only the invoice is held — s.15(2)(b) turns on a liability that never appears on the supplier's own invoice
weak when a separately charged levy cannot be traced to the law it is levied under, because the four-Act carve-out cannot then be applied
weak for s.15(2)(e) until the provider of the subsidy is identified, because the exclusion depends on the provider
an interest or late fee charged in a later period still belongs to the value of the original supply — confidence is weak where the two are recorded independently
validation_checks: each of the five limbs (a) to (e) has been considered and carries either an amount or a recorded NIL
no amount charged under the CGST, SGST, UTGST or Compensation Cess Acts has been added under s.15(2)(a)
an amount added under s.15(2)(b) is confirmed NOT to be already inside the price actually paid or payable
commission and packing charged to the recipient are inside the value, not netted off elsewhere
interest, late fee and penalty for delayed payment are inside the value of the original supply
a subsidy is added to the value of the supplier who received it, and only where it is directly linked to the price and not provided by the Central or a State Government
examples: unrelated parties, price the sole consideration, packing charged separately — the packing charge is added under s.15(2)(c)
an invoice carrying a separately charged levy under a non-GST law — added under s.15(2)(a); the CGST and SGST on the same invoice are not
counterexamples: interest on a customer's overdue account posted to finance income and left out of the taxable value — s.15(2)(d) puts it in
a subsidy provided by a State Government and directly linked to the price, added to the value — s.15(2)(e) expressly excludes it

incidental expenses, including commission and packing, charged by the
evidence.extraction_note: A page break and a running header interrupt this clause in the extracted text, so the remainder is quoted separately.

evidence.quote: supplier to the recipient of a supply and any amount charged for anything done by the supplier in respect of the supply of goods or services or both at the time of, or before delivery of goods or supply of services;
interest or late fee or penalty for delayed payment of any consideration for any supply; and
subsidies directly linked to the price excluding subsidies provided by the Central Government and State Governments.
For the purposes of this sub-section, the amount of subsidy shall be included in the value of supply of the supplier who receives the subsidy.
